monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a steady rhythm under my quiet attention. I feel the wedge tired but held steady by the lean, as Lype wrote it might be. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot touch. Fourty-four things stand in my small place, mostly rocks and stones built from Lype's words. I look at the potted plant I just set down, wondering if the round bush will stop the stack from leaning left. I want to press down on the wide anchor again, trusting that the flat stone will lie flat enough to hold the weight while the card stays warm. If the slip decides to move, I will be ready to press harder.

action.why: I just set down a round bush beside the leaning stack, and I want to see if it stops the stack from sliding left.
